title: A finite local-dimension witness in a nonempty coordinate chart
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be $S$-schemes, let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $e:T\to X$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Set $Z=Y\times_XT$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $a,b\geq0$ and suppose there is an etale $S$-morphism $h:T\to\mathbf A^{a+b}_S$ [def-sbc-affine-space] with $Z=h^{-1}(\mathbf A^a_S)$ scheme-theoretically, where $\mathbf A^a_S$ is cut out by the last $b$ coordinates $v_1,\ldots,v_b$. Assume $Z\ne\varnothing$. There exist an affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, a minimal prime $s$ of $R$, and a point $t\in Z$ over $s$, such that the image of the corresponding point of $Z_s=Z\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ in $\mathbf A^a_{\kappa(s)}$ is its generic point. Here $\kappa(s)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/s)$, a minimal prime is a prime containing no strictly smaller prime, and a generic point means a point whose closure is the whole space. For this $t$, writing $y$ for its image in $Y$ and $x=i(y)$, the local rings satisfy
$$\dim\mathcal O_{Z,t}=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}=0,\qquad \dim\mathcal O_{T,t}=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=b.$$
Dimensions are the suprema of lengths of strict prime chains [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. More explicitly, passage from these local rings over $s$ to their fibre local rings preserves their prime-poset dimensions, and the ambient affine-space fibre local ring at $h(t)$ is
$$\kappa(s)(u_1,\ldots,u_a)[v_1,\ldots,v_b]_{(v_1,\ldots,v_b)}.$$
No Noetherian, reducedness, finite-dimensionality, smoothness, or finite-type condition is imposed on $S,X,Y$ beyond the displayed etale chart hypotheses.

proof.text: Take a generic point t of an irreducible component of Z. The cartesian coordinate square makes g etale. Flat maps send maximal points in the specialization order to maximal points, using lifting of generalizations, so g(t) and its base point are maximal. Choose an affine base neighborhood and its corresponding prime s. Minimality of s follows by reflecting specializations through the affine-open embedding. Irreducibility of the affine-space fibre implies that g(t), maximal in the total space, is generic in that fibre. The residue field of s is a fraction field of R/s.

source.place: Tags 02GO (etale base change), 03HV (generalizations lift along flat maps), 056G (smooth open maps); generic-component selection by G6.

proof.text: Apply the coordinate-subspace generic-stalk theorem to g(t). The cartesian equality identifies its coordinate-subspace image with h(t). This supplies exactly the required normal polynomial prime and ring equivalence.

source.place: Tag 01HV, part (6); ambient coordinate-subspace local-ring calculation, retained from original Steps 3--4.

proof.text: A fibre inclusion is an embedding. At a maximal base point all generalizations of a chosen point remain in the fibre, so the inclusion is strictly monotone and lifts all strict generalizations. Order.coheight_eq_of_strictMono equates fibre and total stalk dimensions. The affine base prime is minimal; its localization is zero-dimensional, so its scheme point is maximal. Apply this fibre equality to Z, Y, T, X and the two affine spaces.

source.place: Tag 01HV, part (6); specialization-chain comparison through the fibre embedding by G6. Minimal-prime localization dimension is Mathlib Ring.KrullDimLE.of_isLocalization.

proof.text: Genericity gives dimension zero for the tangential fibre. The explicit normal local-ring equivalence and polynomial-origin theorem give ambient fibre dimension b. Flat locally quasi-finite coheight invariance for the etale maps g, h, Z→Y and T→X transfers these dimensions to Z,Y,T,X. The pullback relation identifies their images in X. Assemble the witnesses, dimensions and the four fibre equalities.
